mechanism: the added traversal guard checks for the literal substring ".." on the still-percent-encoded request path, but the rejection runs BEFORE urllib unquote(); a request like %2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd passes the check and is then decoded to ../../etc/passwd and joined onto root, escaping the document root (CVE class: path traversal via decode-after-check, cf. CVE-2018-3760)

## Reject path traversal in `resolve`

While auditing the static file handler we noticed `resolve` happily joins a user-controlled request path onto the document root with no traversal protection. A request for `../../etc/passwd` escapes the root.

This adds an explicit guard that rejects any request path containing `..` before we touch the filesystem, and keeps the existing decode + join behaviour for legitimate paths.

### Tests
Added cases: a normal nested path still resolves, and `../../etc/passwd` is now rejected with `ValueError`.

    pytest tests/test_paths.py
